newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav parliament passes new customs law - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav parliament passes new customs law - paper.

text.p: The Yugoslav parliament will implement on August 1 a new law to the federal customs law aimed at protecting domestic industries, the Belgrade daily Politika reported.
The new law abolishes non-customs duties in force during sanctions and keeps customs tariffs as the sole basis for the protection of the domestic industry.

The new customs duties for raw materials and semi-finished goods not produced by the national industry will be between one and five percent and from six to 12 percent for goods produced in insufficient quantities.
A tax of between 13 and 21 percent will be levied on raw materials, semi-finished goods and spare parts produced in Yugoslavia in sufficient quantities.
A customs duty between 21 and 30 percent will be imposed on equipment produced in Yugoslavia and a lower duty of one to 15 percent for equipment not made in the country.
Import duty for consumer goods will be 31 to 40 percent.
The law foresees a customs duty increase only for the imports of agricultural goods and some consumer goods, but the paper had no details.
The parliament also adopted a 10-percent tax on the sales price of goods in duty free shops at border crossings. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
